why_relevant: Generic global event aggregator useful only as a coverage net for HU banking/payments events (e.g. International Payment Forum Budapest) that local sources miss; low reliability on dates and must be verified against organiser sites.

source_name: Hitelintézeti Szemle (MNB journal) – conference reports (beszámoló a konferenciáról)
why_relevant: Publishes written conference reports that reconstruct agendas, sessions and speakers of financial-market conferences after the fact — a durable archive when organiser pages are taken down.

Hungary's leading financial news portal; consistently reports MNB supervisory fines (felugyeleti birsag), payment-law breaches (penzforgalmi jogszabalysertes) and draft regulation with dates and institution names. Confirmed article examples on MNB fines against a large bank and against a financial institution.

Tag page aggregating all Portfolio coverage mentioning the central bank/supervisor; efficient single entry point that surfaces consultations, decrees and enforcement stories and points onward to MNB primary documents.

Long-running Hungarian business daily covering banking, MNB decisions and new legal obligations with deadlines; useful cross-check against Portfolio and often carries government/ministry framing of regulatory change.

source_name: hvg.hu — Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) tag page
why_relevant: Confirmed live tag stream of hvg.hu coverage of the central bank/supervisor. hvg is politically independent and frequently reports supervisory conflicts, consumer-protection actions and bank-fee/regulatory disputes that official channels underplay.
Mainstream Hungarian business/finance news site with daily banking and MNB coverage; good breadth on retail payments, fees and regulatory deadlines affecting banks and PSPs.

Hungarian fintech news site; confirmed article reporting the postponement of new AFR (instant payment) features — postponements/deadline slippage are high-value A3 signals rarely issued as standalone official press releases.
Third Hungarian fintech trade outlet; confirmed news item on postponement of AFR 2.0 functions (QR/deeplink/NFC data entry) with concrete effective dates — direct deadline intelligence for payments.
Retail-finance news portal with confirmed fintech tag stream; covers bank fees, MNB consumer-protection measures and payment product changes from the customer-impact angle.

Comparison-site editorial desk that explains new banking/payment rules and deadlines in practical terms; confirmed to publish as a named author column on hvg.hu, so its analysis reaches mainstream audiences and often predates official summaries.

Pro-government daily; confirmed 2025 story on MNB warning banks to honour the April agreement on account packages. Valuable because it reflects the government/MNB-leadership framing and sometimes reports supervisory pressure before formal decisions.
Major independent Hungarian newsroom; investigative reporting on MNB governance, supervisory failures and bank-sector policy that official and pro-government channels do not surface.

source_name: Forbes.hu / Index.hu gazdasag (secondary HU business desks)
why_relevant: Broad-audience business desks that pick up MNB enforcement and payment-rule changes; low unique value but useful for redundancy and for spotting stories the specialised outlets miss.

English-language payments regulatory intelligence service; confirmed item covering Hungarian regulator fines on key banks for AML compliance failure. Bridges HU supervisory actions into English with regulatory context.

source_name: Lexology — Hungary banking/financial services law-firm alerts
why_relevant: Aggregates Hungarian law-firm client alerts on banking regulation; confirmed 'First-step analysis: banking regulation in Hungary'. Law-firm alerts routinely flag draft laws, consultation windows and compliance deadlines earlier and more precisely than general press, and point to the underlying statutes.

source_name: Baker McKenzie Global Financial Services Regulatory Guide — Hungary chapter
why_relevant: English structural map of who regulates Hungarian banking/payments and which decrees apply (e.g. MNB Decree 36/2017 on payment services, PSD2 implementation). Excellent onboarding/actor-map reference and a pointer to primary legal instruments.

source_name: Getting the Deal Through / Lexology GTDT — Banking Regulation: Hungary (Debevoise-edited chapter, PDF)
why_relevant: Confirmed PDF of the Hungary banking-regulation chapter, including the MNB sanction range (HUF 100,000 to 2 billion) and supervisory powers. Useful baseline for calibrating how severe a reported fine is.

Hungary's main English-language business newspaper; the natural English channel for MNB decisions, bank levies and payment-market changes for non-Hungarian-reading analysts. Not confirmed by this run's searches — treat as high-probability but unverified.

source_name: Hungary Today / Daily News Hungary (English general news)
why_relevant: English-language Hungarian news outlets that translate major MNB and banking-policy stories; low technical depth but useful for keeping an English audit trail of headline regulatory events. Not confirmed in this run's searches.

source_name: Moneywiki regulator profile — Magyar Nemzeti Bank
why_relevant: Third-party English profile of the MNB as integrated regulator; a lightweight pointer to the supervisor's mandate and official portals. Low authority — use only for navigation, never as an evidence source.

Statutory publication platform for every MNB supervisory decision (határozat) and order (végzés): licensing, enforcement (jogérvényesítés), market supervision (piacfelügyelet) and consumer protection (fogyasztóvédelem), filterable by date, sector and decision type. This is the canonical primary record of how Hungarian banking/payments rules are actually enforced, including fines on banks, payment institutions and e-money issuers.

The MNB narrates its significant sanctions here, naming the institution, the fine amount and the specific breach — e.g. payment-law breaches fined at OTP Bank Nyrt., CIB Bank Zrt. and O.F.SZ. Országos Fizetési Szolgáltató Zrt., non-compliance with supervisory obligations by MBH Bank, and immediate prohibitions for suspected unauthorised activity. Faster and more interpretable than raw decisions, and reveals supervisory priorities (which practices are being targeted next).

source_name: Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület (PBT) — Ajánlások és kötelezések
why_relevant: The PBT is statutorily authorised to publish its binding decisions (kötelezést tartalmazó határozat) and recommendations (ajánlás) anonymised, with a short description of the dispute and its outcome. This is the earliest structured signal of recurring consumer-vs-bank/PSP friction points (payment disputes, unauthorised transactions, fees) — issues that typically become supervisory or regulatory targets later.

source_name: Jelentés a Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület éves tevékenységéről (PBT annual reports)
why_relevant: Annual quantitative and thematic breakdown of financial consumer disputes: case volumes, subject matter, which providers comply with recommendations/binding decisions. Best single time-series for measuring where complaint pressure sits in Hungarian banking and payments.

source_name: PBT — Határon átnyúló pénzügyi fogyasztói jogvita (FIN-NET)
why_relevant: Documents the PBT's membership of the EU FIN-NET cross-border financial ADR network — the bridge from the Hungarian complaint channel to peer ADR bodies and EU-level dispute statistics, useful for benchmarking HU complaint patterns against other EEA markets.

source_name: Magyar Európai Fogyasztói Központ (Hungarian European Consumer Centre) — alternatív vitarendezés / pénzügyi békéltetés
why_relevant: Consumer-facing intermediary that channels cross-border complaints (including card and payment disputes) and describes routing between PBT, ECC-Net and FIN-NET. Useful for spotting cross-border payment friction not captured by MNB channels.
